title: Millions of Pounds Lost as England Faces Major Medicine Waste
subtitle: Pharmacy experts warn that unused drugs are harming the environment and the NHS budget.

summary.en: New data shows that England throws away huge amounts of medicine every year. The National Pharmacy Association estimates this waste costs the NHS at least £480 million annually. Experts warn that keeping unused drugs at home can also lead to serious health risks for patients. Pharmacy leaders are now calling for better reviews of repeat prescriptions to solve the problem. Meanwhile, the NHS is using technology and local campaigns to help patients manage their medicine orders more carefully.
summary.zh: 最新數據顯示，英格蘭每年丟棄大量藥物。英國藥局協會估計，這些浪費每年讓英國國家醫療保健服務損失至少四點八億英鎊。專家警告，將未使用藥物留在家中可能對病患造成嚴重健康風險。藥界領袖現正呼籲加強重複處方箋的審查以解決此問題。同時，英國國家醫療保健服務正透過科技與地方宣導活動，協助病患更謹慎地管理藥物訂單。

paragraphs.en: A new report has highlighted a major problem within England’s healthcare system: the massive amount of medicine that goes to waste every year. According to the National Pharmacy Association (NPA), the total weight of unused or partly used medicine thrown away in England during 2024-25 reached 3,400 tonnes. To help people understand the scale of this issue, the group noted that this amount of waste could fill 75 swimming pools.
paragraphs.zh: 一份最新報告凸顯了英格蘭醫療體系內的一個重大問題：每年有巨量的藥物遭到浪費。根據英國藥局協會（National Pharmacy Association, NPA）的數據，二零二四至二五年間，英格蘭被丟棄的未使用或部分使用藥物總重達三千四百公噸。為了讓大眾了解問題的嚴重性，該組織指出，這些廢棄藥物足以填滿七十五座游泳池。

paragraphs.en: This problem is not just about physical waste; it is also a significant financial burden. The NPA estimates that this waste costs the National Health Service (NHS) at least £480 million every year. Olivier Picard, the chair of the NPA, explained that this is money that could be better spent on improving services for patients. He noted that once a medicine leaves a pharmacy, it cannot be given to another person, even if the bottle remains unopened. Because of safety rules, the medicine must be destroyed.
paragraphs.zh: 這個問題不僅僅是實體廢棄物，更造成了沉重的財務負擔。英國藥局協會估計，這些浪費每年讓英國國家醫療保健服務（NHS）損失至少四點八億英鎊。該協會主席奧利維耶·皮卡德（Olivier Picard）解釋，這些資金本可用於改善病患服務。他指出，藥物一旦離開藥局，即便瓶身未開封，也無法再轉交給他人。基於安全規範，這些藥物必須銷毀。

paragraphs.en: Beyond the financial cost, experts are worried about the impact on the environment and patient safety. Dr. Rasha Abdelsalam Elshenawy, a senior lecturer at the University of Hertfordshire, warned that leftover drugs create serious risks. She explained that when patients keep leftover antibiotics at home, they might take them later without talking to a doctor. This behavior can lead to antimicrobial resistance — a situation where germs become stronger and medicine stops working as well as it should. Dr. Elshenawy described this as one of the biggest threats to modern medicine today.
paragraphs.zh: 除了財務成本外，專家也擔憂其對環境與病患安全的影響。赫特福德大學（University of Hertfordshire）資深講師拉莎·阿卜杜勒薩拉姆·艾爾謝納維博士（Dr. Rasha Abdelsalam Elshenawy）警告，剩餘藥物會帶來嚴重風險。她解釋，當病患將剩餘的抗生素留在家中，可能會在未諮詢醫師的情況下自行服用。這種行為可能導致抗藥性，即病菌變得更強，藥物效力減弱。艾爾謝納維博士形容這是當代醫學面臨的最大威脅之一。

paragraphs.en: To address this, the NPA, which represents 6,000 independent community pharmacies, is calling for changes to how patients receive their repeat prescriptions. A repeat prescription is a regular order for medicine that a patient needs over a long period. The organization suggests that patients who take several different medicines should have their prescriptions reviewed more often. These reviews would allow pharmacists to check if a patient still needs all their current drugs or if some can be stopped. The NPA also urged the public to be more careful and avoid ordering more medicine than they actually need.
paragraphs.zh: 為了解決此問題，代表六千家獨立社區藥局的英國藥局協會呼籲改革病患領取重複處方箋的方式。重複處方箋是指病患長期需要定期領取的藥物。該組織建議，服用多種藥物的病患應更頻繁地接受處方審查。透過這些審查，藥師可以確認病患是否仍需服用所有現有藥物，或是否能停用部分藥物。該協會也敦促大眾應更謹慎，避免訂購超過實際需求的藥量。

paragraphs.en: This issue of waste is particularly difficult because it comes at a time when England is already facing supply problems. In June, health leaders warned that the country is experiencing some of the most severe shortages of common medicines on record. These shortages include common painkillers, as well as specific drugs for epilepsy and hormone replacement therapy (HRT). The Royal College of GPs and the NPA have both pointed to long-lasting supply issues for important medicines, such as those used by menopausal women and patients with pancreatic cancer or cystic fibrosis.
paragraphs.zh: 藥物浪費問題之所以棘手，是因為英格蘭目前正面臨供應短缺。六月時，醫療主管機關警告，該國正經歷有紀錄以來最嚴重的常見藥物短缺。這些短缺包括常見止痛藥，以及治療癲癇與荷爾蒙替代療法（HRT）的特定藥物。英國皇家全科醫師學院（Royal College of GPs）與英國藥局協會皆指出，重要藥物長期供應不足，例如更年期女性、胰臟癌或囊腫性纖維化病患所使用的藥物。

paragraphs.en: In response to these concerns, an NHS England spokesperson said that the health service is taking steps to help people manage their prescriptions more effectively. The NHS is encouraging patients to use the official NHS app on their mobile phones to track and order their repeat prescriptions. By using digital tools, the health service hopes that patients will have better control over their medication orders and avoid unnecessary waste.
paragraphs.zh: 針對這些疑慮，英國國家醫療保健服務發言人表示，醫療體系正採取措施，協助民眾更有效地管理處方箋。英國國家醫療保健服務鼓勵病患使用手機上的官方應用程式，以追蹤並訂購重複處方箋。透過數位工具，醫療體系希望病患能更好地控管藥物訂單，避免不必要的浪費。

paragraphs.en: Furthermore, the NHS spokesperson noted that several local services are currently running campaigns to reduce medicine waste. These efforts are part of a wider goal to make sure that medicines are used in the best possible way. The spokesperson added that the total number of dependency-forming medications—drugs that a person can become physically reliant on—has fallen over the last decade, showing that progress is being made in other areas of medicine management.
paragraphs.zh: 此外，該發言人指出，目前多個地方醫療服務單位正推動減少藥物浪費的宣導活動。這些努力是確保藥物獲得最佳利用的廣泛目標之一。發言人補充，過去十年來，會產生依賴性的藥物（即病患可能產生生理依賴的藥物）總量已有所下降，顯示在藥物管理的其他領域已取得進展。

paragraphs.en: Ultimately, the challenge is to balance the need for easy access to medicine with the need for responsible use. Pharmacists are encouraging patients to speak up if they have any concerns about their treatment. By working together, patients and healthcare professionals hope to lower the amount of wasted medicine, save money for the NHS, and keep patients safer. As the NPA suggests, the best way to start is by only requesting what is truly necessary and ensuring that every medicine cabinet is regularly checked.
paragraphs.zh: 歸根究柢，挑戰在於如何在藥物取得便利性與負責任的使用之間取得平衡。藥師鼓勵病患若對治療有任何疑慮，應主動提出。透過病患與醫療專業人員的合作，希望能降低藥物浪費量，為英國國家醫療保健服務節省經費，並保障病患安全。正如英國藥局協會所建議，最好的開始方式就是只索取真正必要的藥量，並確保定期檢查家中的藥箱。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To go away from a place.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（葉子），這裡作動詞用。文中：He noted that once a medicine leaves a pharmacy, it cannot be given to another person, even if the bottle remains unopened.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To organize or be in charge of an activity or campaign.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞（跑步），這裡指舉辦活動。文中：Furthermore, the NHS spokesperson noted that several local services are currently running campaigns to reduce medicine waste.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To express your opinion or feelings clearly and openly.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 勇敢說出自己的想法或疑慮。
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面意思容易誤解為「大聲說話」，這裡指表達意見。文中：Pharmacists are encouraging patients to speak up if they have any concerns about their treatment.

quiz.question: According to the National Pharmacy Association, what happens to medicine once it has left a pharmacy?

options.A: It can be returned for a partial refund if the bottle is unopened.
options.B: It must be destroyed due to safety regulations, even if unused.
options.C: It is redistributed to other patients who have similar prescriptions.
options.D: It is stored by the pharmacy for future use by the same patient.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，Olivier Picard 明確指出，一旦藥物離開藥局，即使瓶子未開封，基於安全規定，這些藥物也不能給予他人，必須銷毀。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章未提及退款；選項 C 錯誤，因為文章明確說不能給予他人；選項 D 錯誤，因為藥物一旦離開藥局，藥局便無法再對其進行管理或儲存。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the relationship between medicine waste and the current medicine supply crisis in England?

options.A: The waste is the primary cause of the nationwide shortage of painkillers.
options.B: Reducing waste could potentially alleviate some of the pressure caused by supply shortages.
options.C: The NHS is prioritizing the production of new drugs over the management of existing waste.
options.D: Patients are intentionally wasting medicine to protest the current supply problems.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第五段提到英國正面臨嚴重的藥物短缺問題，而第一段與第二段指出每年有 3,400 噸藥物被浪費且造成鉅額財務負擔。由此可推論，若能減少這些不必要的浪費，將能節省資金並更有效地分配資源，從而緩解短缺壓力。選項 A 過度推論，文章未稱浪費是「主要原因」；選項 C 與 D 在文中皆無相關證據支持。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the phrase 'speak up' mean in the context of patient-pharmacist communication?

options.A: To talk louder so the pharmacist can hear clearly.
options.B: To express concerns or questions about their medical treatment.
options.C: To complain formally about the high cost of healthcare.
options.D: To request more medicine than what is currently prescribed.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在此語境下，「speak up」意指勇於表達意見或提出疑慮。文章最後一段提到，藥師鼓勵病人若對治療有任何疑慮，應「speak up」（主動溝通），以便雙方合作減少浪費並確保用藥安全。選項 A 是字面意思的誤解；選項 C 語意過於負面且非文中本意；選項 D 與文章倡導的「減少浪費」目標完全相反。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding medicine waste in England?

options.A: The NHS should stop providing repeat prescriptions to prevent any chance of waste.
options.B: Medicine waste is an unavoidable consequence of modern healthcare systems.
options.C: The government must increase taxes to cover the £480 million lost to waste.
options.D: Addressing medicine waste requires a collaborative effort to improve prescription management and patient awareness.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。全文旨在探討藥物浪費的嚴重性，並提出多種解決方案，包括藥師審核處方、使用 NHS App 數位工具，以及呼籲大眾負責任地訂購藥物。這顯示文章的核心在於強調透過多方合作來改善現況。選項 A 過於極端；選項 B 與文章積極尋求解決方案的態度不符；選項 C 在文中未被提及作為解決方案。
